arms.observed: AL: corrected R2=0.9970 vs paper R2=0.9386 (delta=+0.0584). AD: corrected R2=0.9985 vs paper R2=0.9595 (delta=+0.0390). arms.diagnostic_note: All three predictions confirmed. Corrected model achieves R2>0.997 for both AL and AD across all 3 seeds. Paper MAE is 4.4-5.0x larger than corrected model MAE (prediction: at least 2x). Corrected model max residual (0.227ms AL, 0.125ms AD) is 4.9x and 5.6x smaller than paper model. Physics interpretation validated: a=isolated ITL at B=1, a+b/d=asymptotic ceiling.

arms.predicted: TTFT follows a saturating (concave) shape for both AL and AD. AD TTFT growth < 1/3 of AL growth. AD marginals monotonically decreasing above rate ~30. AL shows less clean monotone due to prefill-decode contention.
arms.observed: Both AL and AD TTFT show saturating shape (first-half marginal avg > second-half: AL 1.978 vs 0.913, AD 0.455 vs 0.337). AL TTFT: 29.90->45.26ms (15.37ms range). AD TTFT: 45.56->49.86ms (4.30ms range). AD growth is 28.0% of AL growth (prediction: <33%=confirmed). Neither AL nor AD is perfectly monotone: AL has non-monotone points at rates 110 (43.60ms, below rate 90's 43.88ms), 140 (44.91ms, below 130's 45.61ms). AD plateau above rate 90 (~49.2->49.9ms with minor oscillations). Both shapes are clearly saturating overall.
arms.diagnostic_note: Saturating shape confirmed for both modes. AD growth (4.3ms) is 28% of AL growth (15.4ms), confirming the prediction of <1/3. The prediction that AD marginals would be monotonically decreasing above rate 30 was approximately but not strictly correct: AD TTFT plateaus near 49.2-49.9ms above rate 90 with minor (0.2ms) non-monotone variations (noise-level). AL's less clean monotone pattern due to prefill-decode contention is confirmed. The key mechanism (AD dedicated prefill instances avoid decode contention) is validated.

arms.predicted: AD mode has lower E2E than AL at ALL rates. TTFT penalty (AD-AL) never exceeds 20ms. TTFT penalty decreases with rate (from ~15.7ms at rate=1 to ~4.4ms at rate=150). E2E benefit grows monotonically with rate.
arms.observed: AD < AL E2E at ALL 12 rates (confirmed). E2E benefit ranges from 28.9ms (rate=1) to 254.8ms (rate=150). Max TTFT penalty: 15.66ms at rate=1 (budget=20ms, respected). TTFT penalty generally decreases (15.66->9.61->...->4.21-4.59ms) but non-monotone at rates 90->110 (5.35->6.00) and 130->140 (4.21->4.95). E2E benefit plateaus rather than growing strictly monotone at high rates (130: 254.4ms, 140: 254.0ms, 150: 254.8ms). ITL benefit*127 confirms mechanism: grows from 0ms (rate=1, same ITL for AL and AD) to 214ms (rate=150).
arms.diagnostic_note: Core claims confirmed: AD E2E < AL E2E at all 12 rates (unanimous), max TTFT penalty 15.66ms < 20ms budget. The monotone trend predictions were approximately but not strictly correct: E2E benefit plateaus above rate 130 (~255ms), and TTFT penalty shows minor non-monotone oscillations at high rates (noise-level variation of 0.5-0.8ms). The qualitative direction is correct: TTFT penalty shrinks by factor ~3.4x from rate=1 to rate=150. The ITL benefit grows from 0ms at rate=1 (both modes identical with 1 request at a time) to 214ms*1/127 per token at rate=150, confirming the batch-size-dependent mechanism. Rate=1 shows zero ITL benefit because both AL and AD process one request at a time (batch size = 1).

discrepancy_analysis: All three arms confirmed. Minor discrepancies: (1) TTFT marginals for AL and AD are not perfectly monotone - both have noise-level oscillations at high rates (0.5-1ms), but the overall saturating shape is clear. (2) E2E benefit plateaus at ~255ms above rate=130 rather than growing strictly monotonically, but the direction is correct. (3) TTFT penalty oscillates slightly at high rates rather than decreasing strictly monotonically. These are second-order effects; all primary claims (corrected model R2 dominance, saturating TTFT shape, AD E2E dominance, TTFT budget respected) are confirmed unanimously across all seeds.
